advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the `never_attributed` (display-author) signal with signing state so a fully-signed env is not reported as having 'no usable identity'.
evidence: _seam.py:189-196 `author(fallback='Unknown')` returns git `user.name` or the fallback — a display name, unrelated to author_id/author_sig
The finding text asserts 'Its writer has no usable identity' even when reached via never_attributed on a fully-signed env
advisory.finding: The `never_attributed` branch can flag a correctly-signing writer: `author` is the denormalized git `user.name` display value (falls back to the literal 'Unknown' when git user.name is unset), which is independent of signing (`author_id` + `signing_key`). An env that signs every event but whose git user.name is unset will be reported as UNSIGNED_ENV with the message 'Its writer has no usable identity', which is false for a signing writer.
scenarios: A clone signs every event (author_id + signing_key resolve) but has no `git config user.name`, so every event's display author defaults to 'Unknown' — reported as UNSIGNED_ENV despite valid signing.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard the adoption timestamp so a signed event with a missing/non-int timestamp cannot set `_first_signed_ts` to 0 and disable the dormancy gate.
evidence: fsck_authorship.py observe(): `ts = ts if isinstance(ts, int) else 0` then `if payload.get("author_sig"): ... if self._first_signed_ts is None or ts < self._first_signed_ts: self._first_signed_ts = ts`
fsck_authorship.py findings(): `if not row.events or row.last_ts < adopted: continue` with `adopted = self._first_signed_ts`
The code explicitly defends against non-int timestamps, acknowledging they can occur; such an event still passes Check 1 (valid JSON)
advisory.finding: The signing-adoption gate collapses if any signed event carries a missing or non-int timestamp: `ts` defaults to 0, so `_first_signed_ts` becomes 0, and `row.last_ts < adopted` is never true (all last_ts >= 0). This disables the false-positive guard entirely, causing dormant pre-signing envs to be reported — the exact regression the guard exists to prevent.
scenarios: A signed event file with a missing/malformed `timestamp` field sets adoption to 0, so every dormant pre-signing 0%-signed env (the four the design measured as suppressed) is now reported.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an end-to-end test that runs fsck._scan over a fixture store with a post-adoption 0%-signed env and asserts the UNSIGNED_ENV line appears and issue_count includes it.
evidence: search of tests/ for 'env_authorship' returns (no matches)
tests only reference EnvAuthorshipTally directly (test_unsigned_env_fsck_heldout.py:22,39) and _transform_json (test_unsigned_env_fsck_heldout.py:'from rebar._commands.fsck import _transform_json')
fsck.py:105 'env_authorship.observe(filename, json.load(f))' and fsck.py 'issue_count += len(env_findings)' are the diff's integration seam

ABSENCE: a regression that dropped the observe() call, mis-fed the payload, or omitted the issue_count increment would pass every current test because the tally class and _transform_json are exercised in isolation
advisory.finding: The new _scan wiring for UNSIGNED_ENV is never exercised end-to-end: no test runs fsck._scan over a store and asserts that a silent-env produces an UNSIGNED_ENV line and increments issue_count. Tests drive EnvAuthorshipTally directly and feed _transform_json a hand-constructed line, so the diff's actual integration (env_authorship.observe(filename, json.load(f)) inside Check 1, and issue_count += len(env_findings)) is untested.
scenarios: A future refactor drops or reorders the observe() call in Check 1
The issue_count += len(env_findings) line is removed, silently un-counting the new issue

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a seam test with author_id present and signing_key=None asserting the warning names the missing signing_key input.
evidence: _seam.py:365-367 conditional message: 'no resolvable identity (author_id) for this writer' if not author_id else 'no identity.signing_key configured'
test_seam_logs_when_signing_is_skipped_for_lack_of_identity uses event = {"uuid": "ev-1"} (no author_id), exercising only the not-author_id branch
ABSENCE: no test supplies an event WITH author_id and a config with signing_key=None to reach the else-branch message
advisory.finding: The seam signing-SKIP warning has two message branches but only one is tested: the 'no identity.signing_key configured' branch (reached when author_id resolves but signing_key is absent while the gate/config path is active) is never exercised. Only the not-author_id branch ('no resolvable identity (author_id)') is asserted.
scenarios: A writer with a resolvable identity but no configured signing key on an adoption store — the branch the diff explicitly added a distinct message for

blocking.finding: bugfix-size-attestation: this change touches 167 non-test line(s) — over the 150-line floor for a bug fix — but bug ed5c-42fc-bb7f-4cf4 has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; no plan-review attestation record). A fix this large is a design change wearing a bug label: write the fix plan into the ticket's description, run `rebar review-plan ed5c-42fc-bb7f-4cf4` (it auto-escalates a bug with non-test file impact to the full review and SIGNS an attestation on a PASS; if the review passed but no attestation landed, `rebar sign-review ed5c-42fc-bb7f-4cf4` re-persists it cheaply, and `rebar review-plan ed5c-42fc-bb7f-4cf4 --status` confirms it is current without an LLM call), then re-push.
